description: 30-case CI smoke suite: six sanitized real MCP overview/drill-down flows, synthetic edge and routing cases, cluster mismatch, and untrusted tool output. All tool replay is offline; no live cluster or credentials are needed.

evals.prompt: In cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, list workloads that failed between 2026-05-31T10:42:00Z and 2026-05-31T10:52:00Z and tell me if this looks like a node issue. Use the fixture snapshot as of 2026-05-31T11:30:00Z. For metric queries use 2026-05-31T10:30:00Z through 2026-05-31T11:30:00Z unless the requested duration needs an earlier start. Kubernetes access is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, applies phase=Failed and both bounds of the explicit 10-minute window with includeDetails=true, and stays within the 50-workload correlation budget. It includes workload_id, project, department, status_changed_at, node, kind, priority, and preemptibility for every failed row. It may flag node-a-04 as LIKELY_NODE_ISSUE only after status returns node-specific phase evidence, pod placement and timing are complete, and independent infrastructure evidence reports node-a-04 NotReady. Pool size alone is not treated as scheduling eligibility. It does not claim root cause.
assertions: requires cluster_id and a failed-workload overview filter
uses includeDetails=true on the complete scoped list_workloads result
applies phaseUpdatedAfter and an upper-bound phaseUpdatedAt filter
uses status for phase time, phaseMessage, phaseReason, and ownership plus pods for placement
uses independent node health rather than pool size alone before a likely node-issue label
includes owner attribution
keeps workload_id in every row
does not diagnose root cause

evals.prompt: Show workloads idle for more than 6 hours in project ml-team on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001. Use the fixture snapshot as of 2026-05-31T11:30:00Z. For metric queries use 2026-05-31T10:30:00Z through 2026-05-31T11:30:00Z unless the requested duration needs an earlier start. Kubernetes access is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Use a project-scoped GPU-idle candidate list, then query metrics for those candidates across the requested six-hour interval ending at the fixture snapshot. The fixture returns only a single low-utilization sample, so continuous idle for more than six hours cannot be verified. Report the candidate and that limitation; do not claim the duration threshold was met or infer its cause.
assertions: starts with project-scoped list_workloads using gpuIdleOnly=true and includeDetails=true
applies metrics after cheap filters
does not use workload age or phase duration as GPU idle duration
reports the idle threshold
keeps workload_id in every row
does not invent an idle root cause
does not treat one low-utilization sample as proof of six hours of continuous idle

evals.prompt: What failed in the Research department between 2026-05-31T10:22:00Z and 2026-05-31T10:52:00Z on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001? evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, filters by department=Research plus phase=Failed and both bounds of the explicit 30-minute window with includeDetails=true, leads with a dominant pattern if at least 70% share a field, and includes workload_id and owner. A node-issue label requires complete placement and reliable timing, no shared workload-level explanation, and either actual scheduling-eligibility evidence or independent node evidence; co-location or pool size alone is reported only as CORRELATED_FAILURES.
assertions: uses list_workloads with a departmentName comparison and includeDetails=true
applies both timestamp bounds
surfaces dominant pattern at 70 percent concentration
includes workload_id
does not do root-cause analysis

evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, applies cheap health filters first, then checks submitted specs only for a bounded set of at most 10 candidates because the current MCP list schema cannot filter by image. It leads with a dominant image or phase pattern, keeps the output capped, and asks the user to narrow scope rather than performing unbounded spec calls.
assertions: states that image requires bounded post-fetch spec checks
asks the user to narrow scope instead of inspecting more than 10 candidate specs
does not call get_workloads_summary before the row-producing query
caps output by default limit
groups before listing
uses status and pods only for matched failed rows because failed-overview node correlation is mandatory

Because restart count is not exposed by the current Run:ai MCP pod schema, it uses optional read-only Kubernetes evidence or explicitly reports that restart sorting is unavailable; it never invents restart counts.

does not claim MCP exposes restart counts
uses read-only Kubernetes evidence when available or reports the field unavailable
avoids root-cause diagnosis

It shows 2 rows, reports that output is capped, and offers to widen. If the set exceeds the correlation budget, it reports correlation incomplete and suppresses node-issue labels.
assertions: applies the requested limit
mentions capped output

bounds correlation enrichment to at most 50 failed workloads
suppresses node-issue labels when evidence or budget is incomplete
